items.raw_excerpt: Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen has said she remains confident that the government’s planned cut to VAT on food will be passed on to consumers, dismissing concerns that retailers might absorb some of the saving.
items.summary_en: Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen said she is confident that the government's planned cut to VAT on food will be passed on to consumers. She dismissed concerns that retailers might keep part of the saving for themselves. The cut is part of the government's efforts to lower everyday costs for Danish families.

items.raw_excerpt: Three Otago councils poised to sign a regional deal with the government say they will not do so until they get more clarity around an accommodation levy.

The government recently backtracked on the proposed bed tax, leaving councils uncertain about funding. The delay highlights tensions between local and national government over tourism revenue.

items.raw_excerpt: Skip the security line — for a price. Keflavík's decade-old fast-track lane can now be booked directly by any passenger for ISK 2,480.
